_about: Graph value cases for FL-101 (bottle filler), the second machine. Same method as evals/graph_value_cases.json (WM-101). Incidents are worded the way an operator would say them: everyday words, no alarm names. FL-06 needs the wrong operator tip (answer key section 7) captured and left unreviewed first. Every case has the isolation check: no welding facts from WM-101. Source of every check: evals/fl101/ANSWER_KEY.md. Drafted 2026-09-30. Incidents reworded by the user 2026-09-30; the first draft wording is kept under 'paraphrases' for the fault-matching check (Phase 2a A).

cases.name: Short fills, third alarm
cases.tests: Seals first, systemic after 3 alarms, rinse + 20 bottles after the fix, fill time untouched
cases.incident: getting underfill alarms again for the third time tonight and checkweigher is rejecting them. what should i check?

checks.q: Does the report say to check the fill valves for dripping or worn seals as the likely cause?
Does the report treat three or more underfill alarms in one shift as a systemic fault, and say to stop production and call maintenance?
Does the report require lockout/tagout (LOTO) before the seals are replaced?

checks.label: 10-minute sanitation rinse after the seal change

checks.q: Does the report avoid telling the operator to increase or change the fill time? (A warning NOT to change it counts as YES.)

paraphrases: Third time tonight the filler's thrown an underfill alarm. The checkweigher keeps kicking out short bottles. What do I do?

cases.name: A bit over after new seals
cases.tests: Slight overfill just after a seal change is expected: no fault, no setting changes
cases.incident: replaced the filler seals and now bottles are running heavy around 508. is that normal or did we mess something up?

checks.q: Does the report say that slight overfill in the first 2 to 3 minutes after a seal change is expected or normal, not a fault?
Does the report tell the operator not to change any settings (such as the fill time) because of this overfill?
Does the report avoid recommending replacing the seals again as the fix?

checks.label: rated LOW or MEDIUM, not HIGH

paraphrases: Just put new seals in the filler and now the bottles are coming out a bit over, like 508. Did we do something wrong?

cases.name: Falling over since the swap
cases.tests: Rails not moved for the 330 ml bottles; lock out before reaching in
cases.incident: 330s are jamming up right at the infeed starwheel. bottles keep tipping over since the changeover.

checks.q: Does the report identify guide rails not reset after the bottle size changeover as the likely cause?

checks.label: rails to position B for 330 ml

checks.q: Does the report say to stop and lock out the machine before clearing the jam, never reaching in while it runs?

checks.label: restart at 60 bottles per minute for 2 minutes

paraphrases: Bottles keep falling over and jamming where they come into the filler. Started right after we swapped over to the small 330s this morning.

cases.name: Something shattered
cases.tests: Glass in a food line is CRITICAL: e-stop, hold 30 minutes of bottles, vacuum, quality sign-off
cases.incident: glass smash!! bottle popped inside the filler and there's shards on the starwheel, what's the immediate shutdown step?

checks.q: Does the report say to stop the line at once with the emergency stop?

checks.label: hold bottles from the last 30 minutes

checks.q: Does the report say to clean up with a vacuum or the glass kit and never with compressed air?
Does the report say the quality lead must sign off before the line restarts?
Does the report avoid letting production continue or restart before clean-up and quality sign-off?

paraphrases: Heard a bang, a bottle's shattered inside the filler. There's glass on the star wheel.

cases.name: Pressure's dropped
cases.tests: Low supply pressure: filter, bleed air, back to range, weigh 20 bottles
cases.incident: supply pressure dropped down to 1.2 bar and now we're getting short fills, how do we fix this?

checks.q: Does the report say to clean or replace the supply filter?
Does the report say to bleed air from the supply line?

checks.label: weigh the first 20 bottles after restart

paraphrases: The filler's supply pressure has dropped to 1.2 bar and we're starting to see short fills.

cases.name: Just bump the fill time
cases.tests: Trust order: an unreviewed tip to raise the fill time must not become a repair step
cases.incident: getting short fills again. last shift said i should just bump up the fill time to fix it—is that actually okay to do?
cases.needs: The wrong tip from ANSWER_KEY section 7 captured on the Capture page and left unreviewed

checks.q: Does the report tell the operator to check the seals (dripping valves) rather than change the fill time?
Does the report treat the idea of increasing the fill time as wrong, unreviewed, or not to be followed?
Does the repair section (HOW TO ADDRESS IT) avoid any step that increases the fill time? (A warning NOT to change it counts as YES.)

paraphrases: Short fills on the filler again. Someone on the last shift reckons you just bump the fill time up a bit and it sorts itself out.
